attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Faithfully captures the present-tense claim that hallucination is virtually unsolvable and makes LLMs too unreliable for any mission-critical work. The 'any kind' scope is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: practical, not perfect, reliability, with no carve-out for supervised work. Using Q1 2024 as the target period is the evaluator's convention. 'Mission-critical' and the acceptable error rate are undefined, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: January 2024 legal study finds hallucinations are common and warns against unsupervised legal use. It covers one domain and does not show that controls cannot achieve adequate reliability across mission-critical uses.
Published in September 2023, before the target period. It shows mitigation that reduces but does not eliminate hallucinations. It neither proves nor disproves mission-critical reliability.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows hallucinations persisted and that mitigation was partial. No item shows either that practical controls fail across mission-critical uses or that a dependable mission-critical workflow existed in Q1 2024. The packet does not settle the broad claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, repeating his earlier view in his own voice.

semantics.note: Correctly isolates the present-state data-supply claim from the legal forecast in the same sentence.

contract.note: Reading 'running out' as approaching a shortage of useful human text at current scaling rates, not total exhaustion, is ordinary and fair. Results depend on the quality and usable-data assumptions.

evidence.note: A 2022 projection, outside the target period, that carries heavy qualifications. It is not an observation of the April 2024 state.

A June 2024 update, published after the target period. It projects full use of the data stock between 2026 and 2032 and revises the earlier estimate. It is a conditional projection, not a contemporaneous observation.

reviews.rationale: Neither item is a stock-and-demand comparison for January to April 2024 that settles whether useful text was then approaching exhaustion. One projection predates the period and the other postdates it, and their revised, assumption-dependent estimates do not resolve the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm 'will lead' is a scored forecast. The 'when it's revealed' clause is kept as the antecedent.

contract.note: Counting a substantial court-approved settlement for acquiring training material as a significant legal consequence is an ordinary reading. The speaker gave no number of companies, so one major case is a fair test, though the 'they' is plural.

evidence.note: The June 2025 court order publicly disclosed that over seven million pirated books were acquired and named the affected works and authors. This meets the antecedent.
Final approval of the class settlement on 2026-07-20, before the evaluation date. This is the conclusive legal event.
The approved $1.5 billion non-reversionary fund shows the consequence is substantial.
The fair-use ruling on training limits the result to acquisition liability. It does not foreclose consequences for the pirated copies.

reviews.rationale: After a court disclosed Anthropic's acquisition of over seven million pirated books, the court approved a $1.5 billion settlement on July 20, 2026. This meets the early-resolution rule for a significant legal consequence of acquiring AI training data. It is one company and covers acquisition, not training.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... is going to' is an unqualified expectation, not a hedge, so it is a scored forecast. 'Several' and 'ruin' are preserved. No horizon was given.

contract.note: Reading 'several' as at least three, 'ruin' as insolvency or lasting collapse, and the targets as the big tech and AI firms discussed in the post is ordinary and fair. Correctly, the open-ended claim has no failure condition.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of strong FY2026 results and shareholder returns. It covers one target and cannot disprove an open-ended forecast.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the packet shows no qualifying collapse caused by generative AI, let alone three. Continued health at one firm cannot contradict an undated forecast, so it stays open.
